parsed.summary: The Lean target asserts that some group G (in Type) is finitely presented and not sofic. Sofic is a bespoke definition by finite permutation approximations with normalized Hamming distance, and it matches the standard definition. The main caveat is coverage. The paper's Theorem 1.1 names a specific group, the unit group L_{F2}(1,2)^×, while Lean only proves existence of an unnamed nonsofic group. Lean also adds that this group is finitely presented, a property the excerpt never states for L_{F2}(1,2)^×.

glossary.plain: d_H(p,q) = |{y : p y ≠ q y}| / |Y| for permutations p,q of a finite set Y
glossary.note: Dividing by |Y| = 0 gives junk only when Y is empty; every use here has Y = Fin size with size > 0.

glossary.plain: A positive integer n and an arbitrary map σ: G → Sym(n) with σ(1) = id
glossary.note: Requiring σ(1) = 1 is a standard, harmless normalization.

glossary.plain: For all g,h ∈ F, d_H(σ(gh), σ(g)σ(h)) < ε; and for all g ∈ F with g ≠ 1, d_H(σ(g), id) > 1-ε
glossary.note: Perm multiplication is composition, so σ(g)σ(h) = σ(g)∘σ(h), as in the standard definition.

glossary.plain: For every finite F ⊆ G and every 0<ε<1 there is an (F,ε)-good permutation model
glossary.note: The restriction ε<1 is harmless because the condition is monotone in ε. Countability is not required, but this is consistent with the local definition.

lean_claims.plain: There exists a group G that is finitely presented (Mathlib Group.IsFinitelyPresented) and is not sofic in the sense defined above.

paper_claims.plain: The unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra L_{F2}(1,2) is not sofic.

coverage.why: Lean proves existence of some finitely presented nonsofic group. It does not identify that group as L_{F2}(1,2)^×. Finite presentation is an additional claim not in the excerpt.

flags.explanation: The theorem is existential and does not tie the witness to the Leavitt unit group. It certifies that some nonsofic group exists, not the paper's specific statement. It also asserts finite presentation, which the excerpt does not state for L_{F2}(1,2)^× (not in excerpt). This could stem from a different part of the paper or from a known fact.
flags.probe_idea: Define the Leavitt algebra over ZMod 2 as a RingQuot of a FreeAlgebra and state ¬ SoficGroups.Sofic (RingQuot ...)ˣ.

flags.explanation: This is a bespoke definition rather than a Mathlib one. Read carefully, it matches the standard definition: arbitrary maps, σ(1)=1, multiplicativity defect < ε, non-identity elements moving more than a (1-ε) fraction of points. It is neither trivially false nor too strong, so non-soficity here is genuine non-soficity.
flags.probe_idea: Prove Sofic for a finite group, e.g. Sofic (Multiplicative (ZMod 3)), via the regular representation, to confirm the definition is satisfiable.

lint_verdicts.why: In every use Y = Fin M.size with size_pos, so the denominator is nonzero.
ε is real, so 1 - ε is real subtraction with no truncation.
